# Navigation app names — brand terms (Round 87)

Reviewed November 24, 2026 (America/New_York) from official public sources only.

**Decision: no Google Maps, Apple Maps, or Waze logos or icons are used in FINEST HQ.**
App names stay as plain text labels everywhere they appear (7a Navigate, Other picker,
9o Default navigation chips, map sheets, directory cards, entry forms, 1e, and related
surfaces). No unofficial, redrawn, or third-party copies of those logos are stored here.

This folder is reserved for official brand assets downloaded from each brand's own asset
page if a later review finds a permitted, publicly licensed file for this use. None were
found for this review. Do not add invented or unofficial logo files.

---

## Google Maps — not permitted for this use (text only)

Official sources:

- [Google Geo Guidelines](https://about.google/intl/eng/brand-resource-center/products-and-services/geo-guidelines/)
  (also [en-US](https://about.google/intl/en-US_ALL/brand-resource-center/products-and-services/geo-guidelines/))
- [Brand Resource Center — Guidance](https://about.google/brand-resource-center/guidance/)
- [Brand Resource Center — APIs / product co-branding](https://about.google/brand-resource-center/guidance/apis/)
- [Maps JavaScript API policies (attribution assets)](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/policies)
- [Partner Marketing Hub](https://partnermarketinghub.withgoogle.com/)

Quotes and rules:

- Linking with text is explicitly allowed: "You're also welcome to link to Google Maps with text or a button on your website, such as 'View on Google Maps' or 'Open with Google Maps.'" (Geo Guidelines, Web and apps.) That permission is for a text or button link, not a grant to place the Google Maps logo on our buttons.
- Logos are listed among Google trademarks (the "Google Maps logo" and "Google Maps red pin element"). "You may only use approved versions of our marks, and you must follow all of the general trademark usage guidelines…" (Geo Guidelines, Use of trademarks.)
- Product icons are in the "Ask first" category: "Refer to our icon usage guidelines to see whether you can use certain product icons in association with your business." (Brand Resource Center Guidance.) A public "icon usage guidelines" page was not found at a guessable Brand Resource Center URL (https://about.google/brand-resource-center/guidance/product-icons/ returned 404 on this date).
- The same Guidance page lists "Use Google in plain text" and "Link to our content… maps, etc. using hyperlinks" under "Go for it" (no request needed). It also says: "Don't use the Google logo or any of our brand elements in any way that implies affiliation, endorsement, or sponsorship where such a relationship does not exist."
- API / product co-branding: "Use plain text." and "Use product icons only when necessary." Official product-icon files and more detailed guidance sit in the Partner Marketing Hub, which requires a Google partnership / signed-in account: "If your company has an official brand partnership, make sure you're signed into the Partner Marketing Hub for more detailed guidance and assets."
- The downloadable Google Maps wordmarks and logos on the Maps Platform policies page are **attribution assets** for crediting Google Maps Platform *content*. They have a required height of 16–19 dp and clear space (10 dp left/right/top, 5 dp bottom), must not be modified, and must come from official files. FINEST HQ Navigate buttons do not display Maps Platform map content; using those attribution files as 16–18px leading icons next to the product name would be a different use than the one those assets license.

Because this app is not a Google partner, no official public product-icon package licensing this UI use was found, and product-icon use is an "Ask first" request, **Google Maps stays text-only**.

## Apple Maps — not permitted (text only)

Official sources:

- [Guidelines for Using Apple Trademarks and Copyrights](https://www.apple.com/legal/intellectual-property/guidelinesfor3rdparties.html)
- [Apple Maps Terms and Conditions](https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/maps/terms-en.html)
- [App Store Marketing Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/marketing/guidelines/) (App Store badges only)

Quotes and rules:

- Unauthorized Use §2: "You may not use the Apple Logo or any other Apple-owned graphic symbol, logo, or icon on or in connection with web sites, products, packaging, manuals, promotional/advertising materials, or for any other purpose except pursuant to an express written trademark license from Apple, such as a reseller agreement."
- Authorized Use §2 (Compatibility) allows *word marks* only: "Developers may use Apple, Macintosh, iMac, or any other Apple word mark (but not the Apple Logo or other Apple-owned graphic symbol/logo) in a referential phrase…"
- No official Apple Maps badge or icon for "Open in Apple Maps" was found on Apple's public trademark or marketing pages. App Store badges are for promoting apps on the App Store, not an Apple Maps icon license. The Apple Maps Terms do not grant a trademark or logo license to third-party sites.

**Apple Maps stays text-only.** The word mark "Apple Maps" is used referentially as a label on links that open Apple Maps.

---

## Waze — not permitted (text only)

Official sources:

- [Waze Terms of Use](https://support.google.com/waze/answer/12373727?hl=en) (page last modified July 8, 2026)
- [Waze Brand Center → Partner Marketing Hub](https://www.waze.com/discuss/t/transition-from-waze-brand-center-to-partner-marketing-hub/297345)
- [Waze Deep Links](https://developers.google.com/waze/deeplinks)
- [How to give Waze attribution (Partners)](https://support.google.com/waze/partners/answer/10618825?hl=en)
- [Partner Marketing Hub](https://partnermarketinghub.withgoogle.com/)

Quotes and rules:

- "The Waze brand name and logos are the property of Waze or its affiliates. You should not use Waze branding or logos in a way that is not authorized by these Terms, without Waze's express prior written consent." (Waze Terms of Use.)
- Official Waze brand assets were moved off the public Brand Center and now require a Partner Marketing Hub account and approval.
- The Deep Links documentation explains how to open Waze with a URL; it does not provide a logo or a license to use one.
- Partner attribution rules apply to partners displaying Waze *data*, and even there: "Any other attribution or use of the Waze Brand Features must be pre-approved by Google." This app is not a Waze data partner and has no such approval.

**Waze stays text-only.** The word "Waze" is used as a label on links that open Waze.

---

## What this means in the app

- Keep the existing text labels: "Google Maps", "Apple Maps", "Waze", and 7a's "Navigate with <app>".
- Do not invent, redraw, trace, or download unofficial copies of these logos.
- If a brand later publishes a public official asset and written permission that covers this "open in <app>" UI use, place only that official file here with a note of the source URL and the rules (minimum size, no modification, clear space), then wire it up in the shared nav label helper.
